title: A team steers its taste, and not the method

statements.says: Where teams really differ, the Plugin's opinion is a default a team can edit.
Where the opinion is how Skillworks works, it is Machinery and no team edits it.
One page lists both Steering and Machinery, so a team knows which is which without reading every skill.
Which comments a sweep keeps and which it cuts is Steering, held in the comments rule and owned by the team.
Which code smells a review looks for is Steering, held in the smell baseline.
The shape and size of a ticket is Steering, held in the tracker docs.
The rules, the Suite, the Tracker and the Target branch are Steering.
Steering is seeded into the repo and owned by the team.
The three review axes and "cite it or drop it" are Machinery, the same in every repo.
The test-first loop in tdd is Machinery.
The deep-module view in codebase-design is Machinery.
The plain writing in unslop, and the forced output style, are Machinery.
The Session trailer on every commit, and auto-memory switched off, are Machinery.
The fixed parts are what make Skillworks easy to pick up for a team new to Claude.
Making every opinion a lever was rejected, because a team would own a file for each one and Skillworks would keep no method of its own.

Reading the team's file first and falling back to the Plugin's was rejected, because what a session loads would then change with the Plugin version and no commit, a trade an earlier decision had already turned down.
A later note says the two lists record the decision as it was made, and the Steering page keeps the current lists.
